citation.label: 1.20 E-Filing for Attorneys in Civil Cases
citation.quote: PROPOSED ORDERS

items.review_scope: Pages 1–4 practical filing standards; dated transitional guidance, not a determination of current controlling law.
items.summary: Follow division procedures for proposed orders; the order describes erroneously filed proposed orders going to the pending queue. Separate cases require separate transactions and documents must be distinct items. Civil cover sheet and confidentiality notice are separate documents. Mail-service envelopes go to the serving court or clerk. The order states five days to correct nonconforming pending-queue submissions.

citation.label: 1.30 Notice of Appearance Requirements
citation.quote: Such “coverage” attorney

items.review_scope: Pages 1–3 general appearance, coverage and withdrawal; appendix collected, no specialized family review.
items.summary: Recognized counsel must file the initial pleading, obtain substitution or file an appearance. Coverage counsel files an appearance, subject to the same-firm exception where the firm signed the initial pleading or appearance. Civil limited-appearance termination must be filed. Sole nonsubstantive-continuance appearances have an exception. Withdrawal motions include reasons and the client’s last-known address, phone and email.

citation.label: 3.06 Retention of Documents Filed in Civil Case
citation.quote: must retain all mortgages, notes, and lost

items.review_scope: Pages 1–2 original-document custody only; no foreclosure litigation recipe.
items.summary: Clerks retain original mortgages, notes and lost-note bonds filed in civil cases. Return, destruction or sending requires an order except the disposal/return provisions stated in this order; consult the original for conditional retention periods.

citation.label: 3.09 Standing Case Management Order in County and Circuit Civil Cases
citation.quote: The Clerk shall not accept a civil case for filing

items.review_scope: Pages 1–2 applicability and initial filing; appendix paragraph 11 conferral, pages 4–5. Other appendix deadlines collected but not substantively abstracted.
items.summary: Applies to civil actions except Rule 1.200(a) exclusions. The plaintiff signs and files the standing case-management order with the complaint and serves it on named defendants; the clerk is directed not to accept filing without it. Appendix paragraph 11 requires substantive good-faith conferral before any motion, with date/time certification; an unsuccessful-attempt statement must detail at least three attempts within the immediately preceding one-month period. Original contains track and schedule details.

citation.label: 1.15 Americans With Disabilities Act: Grievance Procedures and Court Notices
citation.quote: All communications which provide notice of court proceedings

items.review_scope: Accommodation request and court-notice provisions pages 1–2 and 4–5; grievance mechanics collected, not substantively analyzed.
items.summary: Requests may be oral or written to the ADA coordinator, without case merits. The order lists 352-337-6237 and Room 410, 201 East University Avenue. Court-proceeding notices must include the prescribed accommodation statement in bold 14-point Times New Roman or Courier; it includes relay 711. Use the source for exact notice text.

citation.label: 9.07 Duty Judge and Emergency Hearing Procedure
citation.quote: HOURS

items.review_scope: Duty-judge availability and referral scope pages 1–2; status page 3. Criminal/domestic-violence mechanics not analyzed.
items.summary: The dated order provides duty-judge access after hours, weekends, holidays and courthouse closures for emergency matters; the duty judge decides whether other requests qualify. This is a shared availability baseline, not a current duty calendar or named on-call contact.

citation.label: 9.08 Procedure for Coverage of Emergency Hearings During the Absence of the Assigned Judge
citation.quote: The judicial assistant will secure

items.review_scope: Pages 1–2 emergency-hearing office routing and date.
items.summary: When the assigned judge is absent, contact that judge’s judicial assistant for a referral. The referral judge decides urgency and that office schedules the hearing. If both judge and assistant are absent, Court Administration routes the request. Do not approach other judges directly outside the stated referral route.
